notes.title: Project NexOS Is Coming to Steam – Follow Development!
notes.content:
It’s been a while since my last development update over on itch.io ([url=https://mrdkoz.itch.io/project-nexos]here[/url]), but rather than posting about every small milestone, I wanted to wait until I had something substantial to share.

Since last year’s update on the StoryImporter, I’ve made major progress: the draft introduction to the story is now fully playable. This required significant refactoring of the original systems, but the result is a much more modular and expandable codebase.

My main focus since then has been on the event system and the Messenger app where most of the interaction with NPCs takes place. This has included features like:
[list]
[*] A typing indicator for better immersion
[*] Simulated reading and typing speeds based on message length
[*] Smart message grouping (i.e., combining sequential messages in the same chat bubble)
[*] A reputation system unlocking dialogue based on player choices
[*] An information system that remembers player discoveries and choices
[*] Player actions outside the messenger influencing NPC responses
[/list]
A core design decision behind all of this is to keep the game entirely data-driven. No event logic is hardcoded: every message, response, and action is stored and managed via the database. This makes it easy to iterate on the story using [url=https://obsidian.md/canvas]Obsidian Canvas[/url] and even major narrative changes can be imported via the StoryImporter without touching the core game logic.

While there’s still more work to do on this system and let’s be honest, it’ll need further additions and polish as development continues but at this moment in time I’m really happy with the current state. It’s exciting to finally have the foundation of a solid, non-linear story engine in place.

Creating the store page on Steam is also a huge milestone. I fully intend to take advantage of the platform’s features, including achievements and Steam Cloud support at the very least.

And finally looking ahead, one of the next big systems I’ll be tackling is accessibility. Project NexOS is inherently a text-heavy game, and that brings its own challenges I don't see these as optional. 

As I make more progress I'll be sure to keep posting updates. In the meantime feel free to add to the discussion below and maybe even add Project NexOS to your wishlist.

Exciting times ahead!
